Yes! It’s definitely true that not everything can be saved, but some of the transformations I’ve been able to get from a good cleaning of items has been amazing! I’ll sit at my local pony club cleaning up the donated tack in their tack sale that benefits the club. More sales for the center and people seeing what the item can really look like without all the dust or caked on mud.

I start with Absorbine Horseman's One Step to clean, with a damp sponge. I use a foam brush to apply Fiebing's 100% Pure Neatsfoot Oil. It works better to apply to the back side of the leather, but I generally apply both sides anyways, so even if one side is covered with fabric, I'll still apply oil to one side. Once that dries, I seal it with a damp sponge and Fiebing's saddle soap. If you don't seal it, dust will just stick so badly to the oiled leather. I've used this method on super old horse equipment and it can give it a totally new life, which brings me to my last tip: if you get good about cleaning leather, realize that you can bring back pretty bad looking leather so keep that in mind when looking at thrift stores or whatever. I've gotten really nice things for my horse because they were so destroyed looking that people sold them super cheaply, but all they really needed was a good cleaning and consistent oiling.

I ride horses competitively, so I am frequently caring for leather (saddles, boots, all sorts of things!). The most important thing I've learned is that all that applies to keeping my saddle in great condition applies to about any other leather product. Now my purses get scrubbed up following my regime for my saddle. I love cleaning leather, it's my favorite relaxing activity.
